conceptual assets.concept: Register-file writeback value produced by the core (rf_wdata)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The core computes the register-file writeback value as rf_wdata <= alu_res or lsu_rdata or csr_rdata or ctrl.pc_ret and provides it to the regfile instance as rd_i (neorv32_cpu_regfile_inst port map rd_i => rf_wdata). The correctness (integrity) of this computed value is required for correct register writes. rf_wdata is computed in this entity from sources produced by ALU, LSU, CSR/control.

conceptual assets.concept: Control bus CSR request fields (ctrl.csr_we, ctrl.csr_re, ctrl.csr_addr, ctrl.csr_wdata)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The control unit drives CSR request fields on the control bus (neorv32_cpu_control port map ctrl_o => ctrl) and the ICC/other submodules consume those fields (neorv32_cpu_icc port map csr_we_i => ctrl.csr_we, csr_re_i => ctrl.csr_re, csr_addr_i => ctrl.csr_addr, csr_wdata_i => ctrl.csr_wdata). Integrity of these control fields is required so CSR accesses and side-effecting control operations follow the implemented control decisions.

conceptual assets.concept: Aggregate CSR readback value presented to control (xcsr_res)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The architecture forms CSR readback data by xcsr_res <= xcsr_cnt or xcsr_alu or xcsr_pmp or xcsr_icc and supplies it into the control unit (neorv32_cpu_control port map xcsr_rdata_i => xcsr_res). Integrity of xcsr_res is required so CSR read returns delivered to control (and thus to software or writeback) reflect the actual CSR sources. xcsr_res is computed here from the component xcsr_* vectors provided by counters, ALU, PMP, ICC.

conceptual assets.concept: CSR read data output from control (csr_rdata)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The control unit exports CSR read results as csr_rdata (neorv32_cpu_control port map csr_rdata_o => csr_rdata) and that signal is used as one source of register-file writeback (rf_wdata). Integrity of csr_rdata is required so register writeback and software-visible CSR results reflect the implemented reads.

The ALU produces the address signal alu_add (neorv32_cpu_alu port map add_o => alu_add) which is forwarded to the load/store unit and PMP (neorv32_cpu_lsu_inst addr_i => alu_add; neorv32_cpu_pmp_inst addr_ls_i => alu_add). Integrity of alu_add is required so memory accesses and PMP checks use the implemented address values.

conceptual assets.concept: Machine interrupt vector assembled from external interrupt lines (irq_machine)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The entity aggregates the three machine interrupt inputs into irq_machine with irq_machine <= mti_i & mei_i & msi_i and forwards that vector to the control unit (neorv32_cpu_control port map irq_machine_i => irq_machine). The control flow depends on this assembled interrupt vector; its integrity must hold for correct interrupt handling.

The debug-interrupt input dbi_i is provided to the control unit (neorv32_cpu_control port map irq_dbg_i => dbi_i). Integrity of this input is required so the control unit's debug-interrupt handling uses the implemented signal.

When the PMP unit is enabled it drives pmp_fault (neorv32_cpu_pmp_inst port map fault_o => pmp_fault) and the control unit consumes it (neorv32_cpu_control port map pmp_fault_i => pmp_fault). Integrity of pmp_fault is required so protection faults are reported and acted on according to the implemented control flow.

If ICC_EN is true the ICC instance drives the external transmit interface (neorv32_cpu_icc port map icc_tx_o => icc_tx_o); when ICC_EN is false the architecture drives icc_tx_o <= icc_terminate_c. icc_tx_o is the exit port through which the ICC submodule communicates externally; integrity of these transmitted values matters to the ICC transmit flow implemented by the RTL.
